solutions.check: grid and clues read from the Guardian's printable copy, its numbering matching the numbers printed in it and the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Jerk given trashy stuff to read after school

blocks.note: SCH is a standard abbreviation for school
muck is filth or worthless rubbish

explanation.surface: A fool is handed some trashy reading matter after lessons end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to read after' tells you the trashy stuff comes after the school abbreviation in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Schmuck is Yiddish-derived slang for a contemptible or foolish person, just as jerk is in American usage.

clue.text: What road builder levels first, having dug baser ground

indicators.note: ground means crushed and broken up, so these letters are broken and reformed

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A road builder levels the land first, having excavated the lower ground beneath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' looks like soil in the scene, but it is the past tense of grind.
explanation.definitionFit: The subgrade is the levelled native soil on which a road's foundation layers are laid, prepared before anything else.

clue.text: Coach players missing second half

indicators.note: with its back half missing, a word keeps only its front five letters

blocks.note: the characters are the people playing parts in a drama

explanation.surface: A team trainer finds that half the side has failed to turn up after the break.
explanation.walkthrough: Coach is not a trainer but a bus; chara is a short form of charabanc.
explanation.definitionFit: A chara is a clipped form of charabanc, an old open motor coach used for outings.

clue.text: Heads of monarchs upon form of coin such as a lepton

definitions.note: an adjective for a particle of the muon kind

indicators.note: the heads of words are their first letters
a different form of a word is a new shape for the same letters

blocks.note: the first letters of monarchs and upon
taken as written

explanation.surface: Royal portraits stamped on a coin, here an old Greek one called a lepton.
explanation.walkthrough: A lepton was a small Greek coin, which suits the surface, but in physics it is a class of particles that includes the muon.
explanation.definitionFit: Muonic means relating to the muon, an elementary particle belonging to the lepton family alongside the electron.

clue.text: One of the Roma French alienated in part

indicators.note: only a part of the words is used, so the answer is a stretch inside them

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of French and the start of alienated

explanation.surface: A Romani person in France has been made to feel partly estranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Chal is a Romani word for a man or fellow, used by Romani people of one of their own.

clue.text: Subterranean channel, a brook that flows north

indicators.note: a flowing stream keeps shifting, so these letters move into a fresh arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
N is the standard abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: An underground watercourse is described as a stream running northward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that' reads like a link word, but its letters belong to the fodder too.
explanation.definitionFit: A katabothron is a swallow hole or underground channel through which water drains in limestone country.

clue.text: Tree circle supplying strips of wood for builders

blocks.note: the fir is a coniferous tree
a ring is a circle

explanation.surface: A ring of trees provides timber battens for a building site.
explanation.definitionFit: Firring, or furring, is the thin strips of wood fixed to joists or walls by builders to level a surface.

clue.text: Pretty boy: 'pathic' is synonymous? Not wholly

indicators.note: only part of the run of words is used, so the answer sits inside them

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of pathic, all of is, and the start of synonymous

explanation.surface: A dictionary-style remark that one old insult for an effeminate youth is nearly equivalent to another.
explanation.walkthrough: Pathic is an archaic word for a passive partner, so the surface pretends to compare two insults.
explanation.definitionFit: A cissy is an effeminate or soft boy, which is the sneering sense of pretty boy.

clue.text: Malefactor, deep dyed perhaps, son disowned

indicators.note: a disowned child is cast out of the family, so that part is removed

blocks.note: crimson is a deep red dye colour, one example of a deep dye
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dyed-in-the-wool wrongdoer is cut off by his family, his son disowned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deep dyed' suggests an incorrigible villain, but it points to a strong red colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Crim is Australian and British slang shortening of criminal, a person who does wrong.

clue.text: I might be X or Y and confused in sexual activity

definitions.text: I might be X or Y
definitions.note: I stands for the answer itself

indicators.note: confused letters are muddled, so they are put in a new order
one item placed in another sits inside its letters

blocks.note: it is a coy word for sex
taken as written

explanation.surface: A puzzled speaker muses on sex, wondering whether their own chromosomes are X or Y.
explanation.walkthrough: The I of the clue speaks as the answer, so the definition is the whole statement 'I might be X or Y', and X and Y are sex chromosomes, apt for the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: An idant is an old biological term for a chromosome, and the X and Y are the sex chromosomes.

clue.text: Extinct carnivore savaged bear, tons in truth

indicators.note: something savaged is mauled and torn apart, so these letters are scattered
one item placed in another sits inside its letters

blocks.note: sooth is an old word for truth
taken as written
T is the abbreviation for ton or tons

explanation.surface: A prehistoric predator mauled a bear, weighing tons, and that is the truth.
explanation.walkthrough: The mixed-up bear and T go inside SOOTH, after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The sabretooth was a big cat with long upper canines that died out at the end of the last Ice Age.

clue.text: Trees of a region, like some birches we heah?

indicators.note: heah is hear in a posh drawl, so we must listen to the word rather than read it

blocks.note: silver, as in the silver birch, said with the dropped r of a plummy accent

explanation.surface: Someone with a posh voice is told about the woodland of an area containing pale birches.
explanation.walkthrough: The spelling heah mimics a non-rhotic upper-class English accent, in which silver loses its final r.
explanation.definitionFit: Sylva means the forest trees of a particular region or period, taken collectively, like flora for plants.

clue.text: Indian queens occupying perches up in oriental evergreens (10, two words)

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the word is read from bottom to top
people occupying a place are inside it, so one word goes within another

blocks.note: seats are places to perch
a rani is an Indian queen or rajah's wife

explanation.surface: Indian royalty sit high up in the branches of Asian trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Star anise is a small evergreen tree of China and Vietnam, valued for its star-shaped spice fruit.

clue.text: Tea with product of dairy's for bard's old age

indicators.note: a product is something made out of raw materials, so the letters are remade into a new order

blocks.note: cha is a colloquial word for tea
taken as written, with the s of the possessive

explanation.surface: Tea taken with milk or cream seems to suit the Bard in his declining years.
explanation.walkthrough: The bard is Shakespeare, who used chair-days in Henry VI for the years of old age spent sitting by the fire.
explanation.definitionFit: Chair-days are the days spent in an armchair, Shakespeare's term for the restful period of later life.

clue.text: Don't declare, Billy

definitions.note: the answer read as two words, BAT ON

blocks.note: first meaning: in cricket, a captain who does not declare lets the side carry on batting
second meaning: a billy or billy club is a policeman's truncheon

explanation.surface: Someone is told to keep quiet about something at customs, addressing a man called Billy.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the batting side may declare its innings closed; refusing to do so means you bat on. Billy is not a name here but the American word for a truncheon.
explanation.definitionFit: A baton is a short stick or truncheon carried by police, the same object as a billy club.

clue.text: Religious instruction in syllabus that may be tested

indicators.note: one item placed in another sits inside its letters

blocks.note: a table is a schedule or list of contents, like a syllabus
RI is the school abbreviation for religious instruction

explanation.surface: A school timetable item: religious instruction appears on a syllabus that pupils can be examined on.
explanation.walkthrough: RI is the old British school subject of religious instruction, and a table in the sense of a timetable or list of topics stands for the syllabus.
explanation.definitionFit: Triable describes something capable of being tried, whether in court or by experiment, so it may be tested.

clue.text: Gritty cyst detected inside the old king?

indicators.note: something found inside another thing lies within its letters

blocks.note: GR, Georgius Rex, is the cipher of a King George
a ranula is a cyst under the tongue

explanation.surface: A medical query about whether a lump was found in a long-dead monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: GR stands for Georgius Rex, King George, and a ranula is a fluid cyst beneath the tongue; the cyst sits between G and R.
explanation.definitionFit: Granular means made up of small grains, which is what makes something feel gritty.

clue.text: Turns to tender tree in disordered scene

indicators.note: one item placed in another sits inside its letters
disordered things are out of their proper sequence and must be rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
the ash is a common tree

explanation.surface: A gardener in a messy scene tends a tree with care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tender' looks like gentle care, but legal tender is money, so the definition means converts into cash.
explanation.definitionFit: To encash a cheque or bond is to convert it into ready money, which is legal tender.

clue.text: Artist heading clique, full of enthusiasm

blocks.note: RA, Royal Academician, is a standard abbreviation for an artist
a ring is a close group of people acting together

explanation.surface: A painter leads a tight little circle of friends, all of them keen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading' places the artist at the front of the clique.
explanation.definitionFit: Raring, as in raring to go, means eager and impatient to begin.

clue.text: Store register rises endlessly in good year

indicators.note: without an end, a word loses its last letter
in a down clue something rising goes upward, so it is read backwards
one item placed in another sits inside its letters

blocks.note: G and Y are the abbreviations for good and year
to register something is to record it

explanation.surface: A shop's cash register shows takings climbing without limit in a prosperous year.
explanation.walkthrough: RECORD loses its last letter, the rest is turned round, and it goes between G and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A grocery is a shop selling food and household goods, a kind of store.

clue.text: Two-handled container made of tin, acting as a caddy?

indicators.note: a caddy is a box that holds something, so the tin here holds another word

blocks.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin
what a caddy traditionally holds is tea, implied by the question mark

explanation.surface: A description of a metal vessel with two handles, used as a box for storing tea.
explanation.walkthrough: The tea that a caddy holds is implied rather than stated, so the question mark flags it; it goes inside the symbol for tin.
explanation.definitionFit: A stean is an old dialect word for a large earthenware jar or pot with two handles.

clue.text: Histrio cancan dancing could be this!

definitions.text: Histrio cancan dancing could be this!

indicators.note: dancing letters jump about out of their order and settle in a new one

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A Roman stage actor performing the cancan would be wildly out of period.
explanation.walkthrough: A histrio was an actor of ancient Rome, while the cancan is a 19th-century Parisian dance, so the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something anachronistic is placed in the wrong historical period, like a Roman performer doing a dance from centuries later.

clue.text: Denoting brightest star, North America flag's hoisted

indicators.note: a hoisted flag is raised, and in a down clue raising reads the letters upward

blocks.note: NA is the abbreviation for North America
a flag is a kind of iris plant; the 's is read as is

explanation.surface: A star-spangled description: America's banner is run up the pole.
explanation.walkthrough: Flag here is the plant, the yellow flag iris, not a banner.
explanation.definitionFit: Sirian means relating to Sirius, the Dog Star, which is the brightest star in the night sky.

clue.text: Fine vessel like a sloop, Benin registration?

blocks.note: first meaning: excellent, first-rate
second meaning: a small sailing boat with a jigger mast
a cryptic extra: Benin's international vehicle registration letters are DY

explanation.surface: A boat resembling a sloop is admired, and someone asks whether it was registered in Benin.
explanation.walkthrough: Benin was formerly Dahomey, so its car plates carry DY; read as D AND Y that spells the answer, a third, playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Dandy is colloquial for very good, and also names a sloop-like small sailing vessel with a mizzen.

clue.text: Counsel of yesteryear, aged …, to wit kept inside

indicators.note: what is kept inside another thing is held within its letters

blocks.note: ae., for Latin aetatis, means aged, as on old memorials
viz is the abbreviation meaning namely or to wit

explanation.surface: An old legal adviser, of some unstated age, keeps his wit to himself.
explanation.walkthrough: The dots after aged mimic an age left blank on a form; AE is the Latin abbreviation seen on tombstones before an age.
explanation.definitionFit: Avize is an archaic spelling of advice, meaning counsel or guidance given in earlier times.

clue.text: Dead shark turned up in railroad station

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the word is read from the bottom upward

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for dead
the tope is a small shark

explanation.surface: A dead shark is found on the platform of a train station.
explanation.definitionFit: In American English a depot is a railroad or bus station, as well as a storage place.

clue.text: Tumour, beginning to grow, a labour reversed

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, the only one taken
something reversed runs backwards, so the phrase before it is read from the end

blocks.note: the first letter of grow
taken as written
moil means hard work or toil

explanation.surface: A grim medical note: a tumour starts to grow, and labour is induced in reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: A glioma is a tumour arising from the glial cells that support nerve tissue in the brain.

clue.text: Phlegm displayed by copper immersed in problem? The reverse

indicators.note: a thing immersed in another lies inside it
the reverse of a word runs it backwards

blocks.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A medical puzzle: phlegm turns up where copper was dipped into some liquid problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The reverse' tells you to turn the problem round, then the copper goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Mucus is the slimy secretion of mucous membranes, and phlegm is mucus from the throat and airways.

clue.text: Commiseration? It replaces art in company

indicators.note: replacing means one thing takes the place of another within the word

blocks.note: a party is a company of people
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone sympathises that a computing department has displaced the art class in a firm.
explanation.definitionFit: Pity is sorrow felt for another's suffering, much the same as commiseration or sympathy.

clue.text: This acid is hypothetical heroin, in varying colours

definitions.note: the answer qualifies an acid known only in theory

indicators.note: one item placed in another sits inside its letters
things that vary change, so these letters take a different order

blocks.note: taken as written
H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: A chemistry aside: a drug turning up in shifting colours is only a theory.
explanation.walkthrough: Chlorous acid, HClO2, has never been isolated pure, which is why the clue calls it hypothetical; the H goes after the first letter of the reworked colours.
explanation.definitionFit: Chlorous acid is a chlorine oxyacid known only in solution, so chemists treat the pure acid as hypothetical.

clue.text: Get a load of exercise, no run for a sprinter?

blocks.note: lo means look or behold, as get a load of does
PE is physical education, school exercise

explanation.surface: A coach tells an athlete to watch this training, since it is no run for a sprinter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no run for a sprinter?' is the definition: the question mark flags that it defines by contrast.
explanation.definitionFit: A lope is a long, easy, bounding stride, a relaxed gait quite unlike a sprinter's dash.

clue.text: I plunged into Rhine tributary, not so substantial

indicators.note: something plunged into a river goes inside it, so one letter enters another word

blocks.note: the Wisper is a small river joining the Rhine in the Rheingau
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to diving into a German river that turned out rather thin.
explanation.walkthrough: The Wisper is a little-known German stream; I goes between its P and E.
explanation.definitionFit: Wispier is the comparative of wispy, meaning thinner and flimsier, so less substantial.

clue.text: Sea shore not visible in part of Hackney

indicators.note: what is not visible is missing from view, so those letters are taken away

blocks.note: taken as written
Shoreditch is a district within the London borough of Hackney

explanation.surface: Standing in an inner London district, you cannot see the sea or the shore.
explanation.walkthrough: Shoreditch is an area of east London in the borough of Hackney; drop the shore and what remains is slang for the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ditch is informal slang for the sea, especially the English Channel or Atlantic, as a ditch of water.

clue.text: Liquid mixture unaffected by distillation getting me (almost) or poet drunk

indicators.note: almost all of something means it falls just short, losing its final letter
a drunk person reels about, so these letters stagger into a new order

blocks.note: me is the setter, whose pseudonym is Azed
taken as written

explanation.surface: A chemist's mixture that cannot be separated by boiling gets the setter or a poet tipsy.
explanation.walkthrough: Me in a clue usually means the setter, here Azed, cut short by one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An azeotrope is a mixture of liquids whose vapour has the same composition, so distilling cannot separate them.

clue.text: Mature stylist has penned this, formerly ineffectual

indicators.note: something penned is enclosed as in a pen, so the answer lies within the words before

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of mature and the start of stylist

explanation.surface: An experienced hairdresser or writer has written something that once proved useless.
explanation.definitionFit: Resty is an archaic word meaning sluggish or restive, hence slow to act and ineffective in old usage.

clue.text: Norway sewens cooked for fresh quality

indicators.note: cooked food is transformed from its raw form, so the letters are reworked

blocks.note: N is the international vehicle code for Norway
taken as written

explanation.surface: Norwegian sea trout are prepared in the kitchen to give them a fresher taste.
explanation.walkthrough: Sewens are sea trout, a Welsh word.
explanation.definitionFit: Newness is the state of being recent or unused, the quality of being fresh.
